slot_types.thesis: central thesis / main idea — requires integrating the full movement of the passage
slot_types.primary_purpose: why a discussion, example or paragraph is in the passage at all — authorial purpose, not the structural role it plays
slot_types.undermine_thesis: which new fact, if true, would most damage the passage's central argument
slot_types.structural_function: why a particular move (analogy, concession, example, tonal shift) was introduced; the answer is a structural role, not local meaning
slot_types.contextual_inference: interpret a dense phrase or compressed claim from its local argumentative context
slot_types.application: a NEW real-world scenario (not a paraphrase); identify which mechanism from the passage best explains it
slot_types.stance: the author's intellectual posture, avoiding simplistic binaries
slot_types.except_scan: three options are directly supported by the passage and one is not; the UNSUPPORTED option is the correct answer
slot_types.decoy_escape: directly tests whether the reader escaped the passage's planted early misreading
slot_types.evidence_function: what work an example or piece of evidence does (illustrate, prove, complicate, license)
slot_types.counterfactual_structure: how the argument would change if a specified paragraph were removed or replaced
slot_types.strengthen: which new fact would most strengthen a specified claim from the passage
slot_types.weaken: which new fact would most weaken a specified claim from the passage
slot_types.author_vs_reported: distinguish the author's own view from views the author reports or steelmans
slot_types.closure_reading: what the ending does — why the passage stops where it does and what is implied next
slot_types.phrase_in_context: the meaning of a specific phrase as used in the passage, not in general usage
slot_types.detail_check: a precise factual/claim-level detail from the passage

thesis: Which one of the following best captures the central idea of the passage?
Which one of the following statements provides a gist of this passage?
The passage is primarily concerned with:
Which one of the following best summarises the author's main argument?
primary_purpose: Which one of the following best explains the primary purpose of the discussion of {X}?
The primary purpose of the passage is to:
Why does the author include the discussion of {X}?
The passage as a whole is best understood as an attempt to:
undermine_thesis: The central idea of the passage would be undermined if:
Which one of the following statements, if true, would best invalidate the main argument of the passage?
Which one of the following, if established, would most damage the author's central claim?
structural_function: What is the structural function of {the specified sentence} within the argument?
The author refers to {X} in order to:
Which one of the following best describes the role played by {the specified paragraph}?
contextual_inference: We can infer from the passage that {X} refers to:
In context, the claim that {quoted phrase} most nearly means that:
Based on the passage, we can infer that {X} would most likely:
Which one of the following is suggested by the sentence {quoted sentence}?
application: Based only on information provided in the passage, which one of the following hypothetical cases would best fit the author's account?
Which one of the following situations is most analogous to the mechanism described in the passage?
Which reading of the following scenario best follows the passage's reasoning?
stance: The author's attitude towards {X} can best be described as:
Which one of the following best describes the author's posture towards {X}?
'{quoted sentence}' We can infer from this statement that the author is being:
The author's position on {X} is best characterised as:
except_scan: All of the following are true of {X}, EXCEPT:
The author faults {X} for all of the following reasons, EXCEPT:
Which one of the following options does NOT represent {the characteristics described in the passage}?
Based on information provided in the passage, all of the following are true, EXCEPT:
{X} is a result of the emergence of all of the following EXCEPT:
decoy_escape: A reader who concluded {the planted misreading} would have misread the passage because:
Which one of the following best explains why the impression created early in the passage does not survive the argument?
The passage most directly corrects which one of the following impressions?
evidence_function: What is the purpose of the example used in the passage?
The author cites {X} primarily in order to:
The {study} mentioned in the passage functions to:
counterfactual_structure: If {the specified paragraph} were removed, the argument would:
Which one of the following, if replaced, would most change the passage's argument?
Had the author omitted {X}, the passage's central claim would:
strengthen: Which one of the following research findings would most strengthen the author's conclusion?
Which one of the following, if true, would most support the claim made in {the specified paragraph}?
Which one of the following would best license the inference the author draws from {X}?
weaken: Which one of the following research findings would weaken the author's conclusion in {the specified paragraph}?
Which one of the following, if true, would most call into question the claim that {X}?
Which one of the following findings would most complicate the author's account of {X}?
author_vs_reported: Which view does the author report or steelman rather than hold?
The author of the passage is likely to disagree with which one of the following statements?
Which one of the following positions is described in the passage but not endorsed by the author?
closure_reading: What does the passage's final sentence accomplish?
The passage stops where it does in order to:
Which one of the following is most strongly implied by the way the passage ends?
phrase_in_context: In the context of the passage, {quoted phrase} is best understood as:
The author uses the word '{X}' to mean:
detail_check: According to the passage, why does {X} happen?
According to the text, {X} is described as:
Regarding {X} described in the passage, the author asserts that:

items.name: The Purpose Frame
items.style_note: difficulty alternates question to question; the purpose question sits mid-set, not at either edge

items.name: Classic Gauntlet
items.style_note: difficulty climbs steadily from the opening thesis to the hardest inference at the close

items.name: Cross-Paragraph Weave
items.style_note: seven of the eight questions reach across paragraphs — the widest span in the library; only the detail check stays local

items.name: Inverted
items.style_note: inverted: the whole-passage question opens the set and the parts are interrogated afterwards, against the reader's already-committed reading

items.name: The Ending Interrogation
items.style_note: the closure question comes early and easy; the real weight is back-loaded into the final three

items.name: The Compression Test
items.style_note: long analytical stems, terse options; discrimination lives in the stem

items.name: Tone Split
items.style_note: the stance question anchors a set of otherwise even, moderate demands

items.name: The Verification Sweep
items.style_note: rewards the reader who verifies against the text rather than recognises

items.name: The Decoy Mirror
items.style_note: the planted misreading is not sprung until late — the reader has to have committed to it first

items.name: The Silent Partner
items.style_note: the author's unstated commitments surface only as the questions climb

items.name: Local-Global Ladder
items.style_note: alternates local reading and cross-passage reach, rung by rung

items.name: Structural Emphasis
items.style_note: why each move was made matters more than what it says; uniformly high demand

items.name: Evidence Audit
items.style_note: the set audits what work each piece of evidence is doing; even, moderate difficulty throughout

items.name: The Reported Frame
items.style_note: the author's own view has to be separated from the views being staged

items.name: The Ambush
items.style_note: five gentle questions, then the last three turn sharply — nothing in the rhythm warns of it

items.name: The Load-Bearing Claim
items.style_note: isolates the one claim the argument cannot lose, then attacks it from several sides

items.name: Application Heavy
items.style_note: new scenarios and staged voices dominate; two difficulty peaks rather than a climb

items.name: Sequential Dependency
items.style_note: later questions reward insight built answering earlier ones

items.name: Purpose First
items.style_note: the hardest work is front-loaded; the set relaxes as it goes

items.name: The Half-Turn
items.style_note: the argument is turned half-way and held there; difficulty zigzags across the set

items.name: Deep Drill
items.style_note: two questions drill the same dense material from different angles

items.name: The Migrating Concept
items.style_note: one concept is tracked as its sense migrates across the passage; difficulty rises with the drift

items.name: Counterfactual Set
items.style_note: what the argument would lose if a part were removed; the demand climbs to the close

items.name: The Uniform Field
items.style_note: eight questions of identical moderate difficulty — no rhythm cue about where the danger is
